body.p: Examiner Interview of January 14, 2025
On January 14, 2025, Attorney for Applicant Corey Donaldson and Primary Examiner Megan Anderson conducted a telephonic

interview regarding the outstanding Office Action. The parties tentatively agreed that the amendments to claim 1 submitted herewith overcame the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Regarding the § 101 rejection, the parties agreed for Applicant to formally submit its arguments.
Amendments in General
Claims 20 and 23 have been cancelled. Claim 1 has been amended to further define the subject matter therein, and is supported at least by FIGs. 4a-5e and accompanying portions of the

specification, including but not limited to paragraphs [0133] and [0247] of U.S. Pub. No. 2021/0387073 (to which all following paragraph numbers refer). Similar amendments have been made to claim 18. No new matter has been added.

The Office has rejected 20 and 23 under 35 U.S.C. § 112 as lacking support from the original disclosure. While Applicant disagrees, these claims have been cancelled. As such, Applicant submits that the rejection is moot and requests the withdrawal of the rejection.

Claims 1-5, 8-10, 12, 14-19, 21-23, and 25 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0336827 to Intonato et al. (hereinafter "Intonato") in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0111318 to Evancha et al. (hereinafter "Evancha") . Claim 24 has been rejected as being obvious over Intonato and Evancha, further in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0111318 to Flynt et al. (hereinafter "Flynt").
Claims 1 and 18 are independent claims from which all other claims depend, and as such the below arguments will focus upon these claims.

Claim 1 has been rejected as being obvious over Intonato in view of Evancha. While Applicant does not necessarily agree, claim 1 has been amended to further define the subject matter therein. Namely, claim now 1 recites a method:

wherein the step of dynamically modifying, based on the configuration instructions read together with the playing of the multimedia content, further comprises recognizing that the value of the at least one first operating parameter that the user has selected is different from the suggested value, and in response to said recognizing, maintaining, by the data processing unit, on said one lateral side of the display module the indication of which of the temporary controls representative of values selectable by the user of at least one first operating parameter of the exercise machine is suggested by the personal trainer in the multimedia content for that phase of the set workout
program

As discussed and tentatively agreed during the Examiner Interview of January 14, 2025, Applicant submits that none of the prior art, including but not limited to Intonato and Evancha, whether taken individually or as a combination, discloses or suggests the method of amended claim 1. As such, Applicant requests the withdrawal of the rejection.
Each of dependent claims 2-4, 7-12, 14-17, 21, 22, 24, and 25 depends from allowable independent claim 1. As such, each of these claims is also non-obvious and allowable.

While different than independent claim 1, independent claim 18 contains similar limitations for which similar arguments apply. As such, Applicant submits that claim 18 is also non-obvious and allowable.
Dependent claim 19 depends from allowable independent claim 18. As such, this claim is also non-obvious and allowable.

Claims 1-5, 8-10, 12, 14-19, 21, 22, 24, and 25 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as being directed to a judicial exception, and more specifically, directed to an abstract idea. Applicant respectfully disagrees and requests that the Office reconsider, at least on the ground that the claims are integrated into a practical application under Step 2A, Prong 2 of the analysis.
Step 2A, Prong 2 asks whether the claim recites an additional element that integrates the judicial exception into a practical application. The Office argues on pages 10-11 of the Office Action

that the claim elements do not "serve to apply the above-identified abstract idea with, or by use of, a particular machine." The Office further argues that the claims "do not add a meaningful limitation to the abstract idea because they amount to simply implementing the abstract idea on a computer." But this is not the case.

Claims 1 and 18 explicitly recite an exercise machine, which is not a generic computer component. Numerous claim limitations are exercise-specific, such as values of exercise machine operating parameters, and suggestions of the multimedia content personal trainer. The claim provides exercisers with various options for their workout via a display module, including suggested options; and the recited exercise machine's settings are modified based on user selections. Moreover, claims 1 and 18 require "physically setting, by the data processing unit, the exercise machine based on the temporary controls made available by the control interface and selected by the user through the control interface in said first operating configuration." The settings of the exercise machine are being physically altered by selections made by a user. This is a practical application.

MPEP § 2106.05 (b) is directly on point. In the Eibel Process case, a natural law that "was applied by a Fourdrinier machine (which was understood in the art to have a specific structure comprising a headbox, a paper-making wire, and a series of rolls)" was found to be eligible. Here, the claims require the components of an exercise machine as would be understood by one of skill in the art.

Beyond the MPEP, additional guidance from the USPTO supports the eligibility of the claims. The following are some of the similar examples from the Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance ("PEG") where claims were found to be eligible:
" PEG Example 4, where mathematical operations were recited in
combination with a mobile device including a GPS receiver, wireless transceiver, and display, and the claim was found to
be eligible.
" PEG Example 23, where a claim reciting relocating obscured
text, and reciting an ordered combination that improved the
functioning of a display, was found to be eligible.
" PEG Example 37, where a claim reciting reorganization of icons
on a display based on frequency of use was found to be
eligible.

By way of example only PEG Example 37 supports eligibility under Step 2A, Prong 2 - Relocation of Icons on a Graphical User Interface. In that example, icons are rearranged on a graphical user interface (GUI) such that the most used icons are nearest the "start" icon of the computer system. There, the claim is eligible because "[t]he claim as a whole integrates the mental process into a practical application. Specifically, the additional elements recite a specific manner of automatically displaying icons to the user based on usage which provides a specific improvement over prior systems, resulting in an improved user interface for electronic devices." Such is the case here-indeed, the recited claim limitations are an even more concrete practical application than that of Example 37. As described above, the claimed method uses the exercise machine components to provide, through a display interface, an improved and enhanced experience. As such, any
judicial exception is integrated into a practical application such that the claims are eligible.

Moreover, claim 18 recites that the "exercise machine is a treadmill, a bike or exercise bike, a rowing machine, an indoor cycling machine, a strength exercise machine, or a station for practicing boxing." These are concrete, practical machines for use by exercisers.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant submits that the claims meet Step 2A, Prong 2 of the analysis, and requests the withdrawal of the rejection.

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are unpatentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application.
Applicant submits that all claims pending herein are in condition for allowance and respectfully requests that a timely Notice of Allowance be issued in this case.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge Deposit Account 60-2598 for any fees in connection with the prosecution of this application.
